issues.description: Bitmap24::set parameter ordering inconsistency: In the template repository header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) the declaration is void set(int i_x, int i_y, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b); whereas the implementation in Bitmap24.cpp (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) defines void Bitmap24::set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b). The example usage in main.cpp (example_program/src/main.cpp) calls bitmap.set(i, j, ...), where i is the row (y) and j is the column (x), which matches the implementation's parameter ordering (i_y, i_x) but not the header declaration. The solution repository shows the header and implementation using the (i_y, i_x, ...) ordering. This mismatch between the template header and the implementation/call sites can confuse students about the API contract (which coordinate is row vs column) and may lead to incorrect implementations or misread code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the declaration in the template header match the implementation and usage. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to: void set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b); and add a brief comment stating the parameter order (i_y = row, i_x = column). Alternatively, if the intended API is (i_x, i_y), change the implementation and all call sites to that order, and update the solution accordingly. Prefer aligning the template header to the implementation/call sites to minimize confusion.

issues.description: Bitmap24::set parameter names/order are inconsistent between the template header, the template implementation, and the solution header. In template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) the declaration is 'void set(int i_x, int i_y, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b);' while the template implementation (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) defines 'void Bitmap24::set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b)'. The solution header (solution_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) uses the implementation's naming/order: 'void set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b);'. A student reading the API (header) will see parameters documented as (i_x, i_y) but the implementation and solution present them as (i_y, i_x), making it unclear which argument is the x coordinate and which is the y coordinate and increasing cognitive load when writing or testing code against the provided header.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template header with the implementation and solution to remove ambiguity. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'void set(int i_x, int i_y, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b);' to 'void set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b);' so the header, implementation, and solution consistently document the same parameter order (first parameter = row/y, second = column/x). Alternatively, rename parameters in the implementation and solution to 'i_x, i_y' if the intended API is (x,y) — but ensure all three artifacts use the same names/order.
